summary: This is a one-page workflow diagram called "Revibe Warranty – Wrong Device", covering the whole process from start to finish. It applies when a customer received a different device from the one they ordered, under warranty. There is no warranty-period check, and the claim goes straight to the original seller (or repair partner). There are four numbered steps. (1) The customer raises the claim in "My Account" (status Pending); labelled NO ACTION REQUIRED. (2) A Revibe agent checks the customer's proof: missing docs are requested, and if they are not provided the claim is Cancelled. Once validated, the status is Pending Collection; labelled NO ACTION REQUIRED. (3) Pickup, labelled ACTION REQUIRED IF SA: for AE & Others the AWB is created automatically (AE = Quiqup, Others = DHL) and the claim moves to Under Collection immediately. For SA the seller must create the AWB manually. For a repair partner it is always automatic (SA = Naqel). (4) Seller action, labelled ACTION REQUIRED: once the Courier Company delivers, the seller can see the claim, its status becomes Under QC, and the seller marks it Valid or Invalid. If Valid, the seller confirms stock of the right device: if available, the correct device is shipped to the customer; if not, an automated refund is charged to the seller (actual cost) and the case is closed. If Invalid, the seller must submit a written reason and supporting proof. Revibe checks it: good proof sends the device to the Lab, and rejected proof means the claim is re-marked Valid (replacement or refund). For a repair partner there is no Lab and Revibe decides. The Lab makes the final decision: Valid means a full refund and ship back to the seller. Invalid means the device ships to the customer if they pay, and is disposed of if they don't. Footer: if delivery fails on ship-back, the agent offers a new AWB; if refused, the device is sent to disposal. All refunds, credits and charges appear in the payment tool. The source is a PDF with no narration, so there were no speech-recognition fixes to make.

terms.meaning: A warranty claim where the customer received a different device than the one ordered. It has no warranty-period check and goes straight to the original seller (or repair partner).

Not defined on the page. It is used for the pickup (auto-created for AE & Others with Quiqup / DHL and for repair partners; created manually by the seller for SA) and for ship-back (the agent offers a new AWB if ship-back delivery fails).
Labels the page uses to split pickup handling: AE (auto AWB, Quiqup), SA (seller creates the AWB manually; repair partner uses Naqel), Others (auto AWB, DHL). The page does not spell out the codes.
An alternative to the original seller that can receive the claim. Its pickup AWB is always automatic (SA = Naqel), and for a disputed claim there is no Lab: Revibe decides.
Status once the customer has raised the claim, awaiting review by the Revibe team.
Status once the Revibe agent has validated the customer's proof.
Status the claim moves to immediately once the AWB is created automatically (AE & Others).
Status once the Courier Company delivers. From this point the seller can see the claim and mark it Valid or Invalid.
Outcome when documents missing from the customer's proof are requested but not provided.
The seller's two options at Under QC. VALID leads to replacement or refund. INVALID requires proof and goes to Revibe review and Lab verification.
The part of the workflow after the seller marks the claim VALID (Replacement or Refund) or INVALID (Proof Required → Revibe Review → Lab Verification).

Makes the final decision on a disputed claim once Revibe accepts the seller's proof. Valid means a full refund and ship back to the seller. Invalid means the device ships to the customer if they pay, and is disposed of if they don't.
Used in the Lab outcome "ship back to seller" and in the footer "Delivery failed on ship-back": if that delivery fails, the agent offers a new AWB; if refused, the device is sent to disposal.
Names given for the automatically created pickup AWBs: Quiqup for AE, DHL for Others, Naqel for a repair partner in SA. The page does not describe them further.
Where all refunds, credits and charges appear.

unclear.issue: The page does not spell out AE and SA (they look like market or country codes), and it does not say which markets count as "Others". Expand them only after confirming with the trainer.
SA pickup: the page says the seller creates the AWB manually but not where or how, by when, or whether the status then moves to Under Collection as it does for AE & Others.
Repair partner pickup: only the SA courier is given (Naqel). The courier for repair partners in AE or other markets is not stated.
"charged to the seller (actual cost)": the page does not define what "actual cost" covers (device price, order value, shipping, etc.).
Lab decision Invalid, "customer pays = ship to customer": the page does not say what the customer pays for (e.g. shipping or a fee) or how much.
Lab decision Valid, "full refund + ship back to seller": the page does not say who bears the cost of that full refund (e.g. whether it is charged to the seller).
"Delivery failed on ship-back": the page does not say whether this covers ship-back to the seller, to the customer, or both, or who does the refusing (the new AWB offer or the delivery).
No deadline is given for the seller to mark Valid/Invalid at Under QC or to submit proof, and no deadline is given for the customer to provide missing docs.
"Repair partner: no Lab, Revibe decides": the page does not say what follows each Revibe decision for a repair partner (refund, ship-back, disposal).

The action labels (NO ACTION REQUIRED / ACTION REQUIRED IF SA / ACTION REQUIRED) do not name who they apply to. They read as seller actions (Step 3: "SA: Seller to create the AWB manually"; Step 4: "Seller action"), but the page does not say so outright.

VALID path, "Available → correct device shipped to the customer": the page does not say who ships the correct device, who pays for that shipment, or what happens to the wrong device that was collected.
